source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed brake tests in a vehicle inspection report

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Make sure to describe the vehicle accurately by including the make, model, year, VIN (Vehicle Identification Number), and license plate number.

3. Date and time of the inspection.
4. Name of the inspector and the inspection company or organization.
5. Details of the failed brake test:
   - Whether it was a routine maintenance test, pre-trip inspection, annual inspection, or post-incident inspection.
   - The brake test method used (e.g., Road Test, Performance-Based Brake Tester or "Rollback" Tester, Decelerometer, etc.)
   - Observations during the test, such as unusual noises, slow stopping response, pulling to one side, brake fade, or any visual evidence of brake system defects.

6. Results of the brake test:
   - If using a Performance-Based Brake Tester, record the results for each axle, as well as the overall stopping distance.
   - If manually testing, note the stopping distance, vehicle
